title: Hermes Agent session document (observed v1)
description: Empirically derived schema for Hermes Agent (~/.hermes/sessions/session_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>_<hex6>.json) session logs, as written by hermes-agent's AIAgent._save_session_log (observed with Hermes v0.6.0 / 2026.3.30). One session is one JSON document, atomically rewritten in full after every turn. This schema describes on-disk observed reality; it is deliberately permissive (additionalProperties: true throughout) because the format is foreign and unversioned. Only fields an importer must rely on are required. See hermes-session.v1.notes.md for linkage invariants, persistence semantics, source-code citations, and known drift in newer hermes revisions.

session_id.description: Session identity. Authoritative over the filename: observed convention is YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6> and filenames are session_<session_id>.json, but the embedded id and the filename disagreed in 1 of 12 observed files (aborted first turn), and the source allows caller-supplied ids, so no pattern is enforced.

model.description: Model identifier as sent to the inference endpoint, at last save. Document-level: a mid-session model switch retroactively relabels the whole document.

base_url.description: Inference endpoint base URL at last save. Observed values include the ChatGPT Codex backend (https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex, driven via the Responses API even though this log stays chat-completions shaped) and local OpenAI-compatible servers (LM Studio, Ollama).

platform.description: Frontend that hosted the session. Only "cli" observed; the source also tags gateway/messaging platforms via the same field.

session_start.description: Naive local-time ISO-8601 timestamp with microseconds and NO timezone offset (e.g. 2026-01-01T12:00:00.123456), so not RFC 3339 date-time. Set once at agent construction.

last_updated.description: Same naive local-time format as session_start. Refreshed on every full-document rewrite (every turn).

system_prompt.description: Full rendered system prompt (persona + instructions) embedded per session; empty string when unavailable. Typically tens of KB. Never appears as a messages[] entry on disk; hermes prepends it to the outgoing API request only.

tools.description: OpenAI function-spec array for the tools enabled at last save (a snapshot; count may vary between sessions). Re-embedded in full on every rewrite.

message_count.description: Writer-maintained count; equal to messages.length in all observed files. Hermes uses it as a no-shrink guard: a rewrite carrying fewer messages than the existing file is skipped. Importers should recompute rather than trust it.

messages.description: Whole conversation in OpenAI chat-completions message shape, in chronological order (array order is the only ordering; individual messages carry no timestamps). First message was role "user" in every observed file; a session may end on any role, including a lone user message from an aborted turn.

role.description: Discriminator. Observed values: "user", "assistant", "tool". Kept an open string because the writer's docstring reserves injected system messages, though none were observed on disk.

user_message.description: Operator input. Observed with exactly {role, content}; transient bookkeeping keys (e.g. a memory-flush sentinel) exist in source and are tolerated.

assistant_message.description: Model output turn. content is always a string, often "" on pure tool-call turns (the writer coalesces null to ""); it may contain literal <think>...</think> blocks for models that inline reasoning. reasoning/finish_reason are present on the normal writer path but omitted on some fallback paths in source, so they are optional here.

reasoning.description: Extracted reasoning/thinking text, or null when the model produced none. Observed union. May duplicate <think> blocks embedded in content.

reasoning_content.description: Rare (1 of 27 observed assistant messages): provider-style duplicate of reasoning, seen with a local OpenAI-compatible backend.

finish_reason.description: Observed: "stop", "tool_calls". Source can also record "incomplete" (Codex reasoning-only turns).

tool_calls.description: Present iff the turn requested tools (1-2 calls observed per turn; more are possible). Each call's id is answered by a later role:"tool" message whose tool_call_id matches.

codex_reasoning_items.description: Codex Responses API reasoning items preserved for multi-turn continuity; opaque to importers.

tool_message.description: Tool result. content is always a string, commonly stringified JSON like {"output": ...}; hermes may append budget warnings, a truncation marker beyond 100k chars, or substitute bracketed synthetic strings for cancelled/unavailable results.

tool_call_id.description: Must equal the id of a tool_call in a preceding assistant message (1:1 in-order linkage; held in every observed file).

tool_call.description: One requested tool invocation. All observed calls carried exactly {id, call_id, response_item_id, type, function} with id == call_id; only id and function are load-bearing for import. Newer hermes revisions may add extra_content (provider continuity blobs).

id.description: Call identity referenced by the matching tool message's tool_call_id. Provider-issued (e.g. call_<opaque>) or hermes-synthesized deterministic fallback (call_<sha256-12>).

call_id.description: Duplicate of id in every observed call (Responses-API bookkeeping).

response_item_id.description: Codex Responses function_call item id, always fc_-prefixed in observed data; synthesized from the call id (call_ -> fc_) for non-Codex backends.

arguments.description: JSON-encoded arguments object as a string (chat-completions convention); the source coerces non-strings before saving.

codex_reasoning_item.description: Opaque encrypted reasoning item from the Codex Responses API, replayed verbatim on later turns. Preserve byte-exact; only summary[].text is human-readable. No field is load-bearing for import.

id.description: Responses item id, rs_-prefixed in observed data.

encrypted_content.description: Opaque ciphertext blob; not decryptable by importers.

summary.description: Human-readable reasoning summaries; empty array observed when the model produced none.

tool_spec.description: OpenAI function tool definition, embedded verbatim. Not load-bearing for import; kept for tool-availability provenance.

parameters.description: JSON-Schema-ish parameter spec: {type: "object", properties: {...}} with required[] present on most but not all observed tools.
